newsitem.title: DUBAI: Sudan vice-president in Saudi for talks on fighting.
newsitem.headline: Sudan vice-president in Saudi for talks on fighting.

text.p: Sudanese Vice-President al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh arrived in Saudi Arabia on Sunday as part of a regional tour to brief Arab leaders on the military conflict in his country, Arab diplomats said.
Saleh and Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha were expected to meet Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah, they added.

Sudan's Islamist military government has called for mobilisation against what it says are attacks from troops of neighbours Eritrea and Ethiopia, rather than rebels. Both states, and also Egypt, deny these charges.
Saleh has already been to Egypt and Yemen and will leave for Syria from Saudi Arabia, the diplomats added.

Ties between Sudan and Saudi Arabia have recovered from strains caused by differences over the Gulf crisis sparked by Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Sudan refused to back a Saudi-based U.S.-led Western military alliance that pushed Iraqi forces out of Kuwait six months later.
The Sudanese opposition says it has seized several towns and garrisons in the Blue Nile area but the government only admits to the loss of Kurmuk and Qeissan near the Ethiopian border.

The rebels say their goal is to advance on Damazin, site of a hydroelectricity plant which supplies Khartoum with most its power, to put pressure on the Sudanese government and bring about a popular uprising.
